post_text:
In 2019: Memphis 20%, Cleveland 22%, Detroit 24%.
Same poverty rates. Same district size. Same odds.
By 2024: Cleveland 18%, Detroit 19%, Memphis 29.6%.

Same starting line. Opposite trajectories.

Five cities entered 2020 with nearly identical profiles. By 2024, two had cut absenteeism by 4–5 points. One had added 9.6 points. The difference was not ESSER money — all five received comparable per-pupil relief.

The difference was the intervention model.

Cleveland and Detroit reached families within 3 days of unexcused absences — before students crossed the 18-day chronic threshold. Memphis ran district-wide awareness campaigns. The data shows what the research already knew: school-level accountability beats district-level campaigns every time. Three specific interventions appear in both recovering cities and in none of the ones that didn't recover.
